text: [urgent] In this world, every time someone talks about you behind your back, you hear a ding. Most people hear a few a day. Leo had never heard a single one. Not one, his whole life. Everyone just liked him.

[urgent] Then he switched schools. And on the first morning, ding. Then two more. Then twenty. Every hallway, every class, every time he walked past. Ding. Ding. Ding. [sad] So Leo stopped talking. He ate lunch alone. He took the long way home.

[sad] For a whole month. [curious] Until one day, the dings got so loud he had to know. So he hid behind the lockers, and listened. [softly] The new kid is SO funny. Why won't he sit with us? [warmly] The rule never said it had to be bad. The next day, Leo sat down, and the loudest ding of all came from her.
